title: Ansel and the Visitor
premise: Theo Eastwick takes a teaching post at Marrowfen School to disappear after a scandal, but the school has a problem: one class per year vanishes, and everyone remembers them differently. The mirrors in her rented cottage lag a second behind reality, and in that stolen second Theo glimpses the missing children, still mid-lesson, waiting for someone to finish the founders' interrupted ritual. As she falls for the school's caretaker, Ansel, who has spent thirty years feeding the ritual just enough memory to keep the children dreaming rather than screaming, Theo must choose between erasing herself safely and giving the ritual what it actually wants: a name freely given. In the end she completes it not as sacrifice but as adoption, pulling the children out of the lag and into the present, at the cost of every mirror in the world forgetting her face except Ansel's.
about_author: Dominic Pemberton is the pen name of a former boarding-school matron who spent eleven years convincing herself the noises were pipes. She writes horror about institutions that love their charges too much to let them go.

chapters.title: The Position Nobody Applied For
chapters.summary: Theo arrives at fog-bound Marrowfen School, hired by a headmistress who never blinks. POV: Theo. She notices the staff roster lists teachers who died decades ago and decides not to ask. Emotional beat: wary relief at finally being somewhere no one knows her.

chapters.title: Class 4-B, Present But Not Accounted For
chapters.summary: On her first day, Theo's register shows twenty-nine students; twenty-two sit before her. The seven empty desks are warm. POV: Theo. A colleague, Miss Halloway, warns her never to mark the absent ones absent. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Ansel of the Long Corridor
chapters.summary: Theo meets Ansel, the caretaker, who polishes the same corridor nightly and knows where every creak lives. POV: alternating Theo and Ansel. He fixes her broken latch without being asked and says the house 'gets lonely.' Emotional beat: unexpected warmth against institutional cold.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: Theo's bathroom mirror reflects her raising a hand before she raises it—no, after; the reflection lags exactly one second. POV: Theo. She tests it with a metronome until 3 a.m. Emotional beat: rationalist vertigo, the first crack in her disbelief.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the archive, Theo finds the founders' ledger: a ritual begun in 1893 and abandoned halfway, its final page torn out. Seven names are written in a column titled 'Held.' POV: Theo. Emotional beat: scholarly fascination shading into complicity—she keeps reading past midnight.

chapters.title: What Ansel Feeds the Dark
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV: each night he tells the walls one true memory of his own, the price of keeping the held children asleep instead of aware. We learn he was Class 4-B once, the one who got out. Emotional beat: guilt worn smooth as river stone.

chapters.title: Miss Halloway's Confession
chapters.summary: Halloway admits she marked a held child absent in 1987; the child woke, and three classrooms emptied that winter. POV: Theo witnessing. Emotional beat: horror of small bureaucratic errors becoming cosmic ones.

chapters.title: The Lag Widens
chapters.summary: The mirror delay grows to two seconds, then five. In the lagged reflections Theo sees the classroom behind her: seven children at desks, watching her back. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: terror mixed with a terrible tenderness—they look hungry for attention, not blood.

chapters.title: A Lesson Through Glass
chapters.summary: Theo teaches aloud facing the mirror, and the reflected children mouth answers to her questions. One girl, Ivy, writes on the inside of the glass: FINISH IT. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: found-family spark; she starts caring which is more dangerous than fear.

chapters.title: Duty vs. Desire
chapters.summary: Ansel begs Theo to leave before term ends—the ritual completes only if a newcomer chooses to stay past the solstice. They argue, then kiss in the corridor he polishes. POV: both. Emotional beat: love declared precisely when staying becomes lethal.

chapters.title: The Headmistress's Terms
chapters.summary: The headmistress reveals she is the surviving founder, sustained by the ritual, and offers Theo a bargain: leave now and forget, or stay and finish it on the school's terms—which require a name given unwillingly. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: coercion dressed as kindness.

chapters.title: Ivy's Second of Silence
chapters.summary: Through the widening lag, Ivy communicates in fragments: the ritual doesn't want a sacrifice, it wants an invitation—but the founders twisted it into theft. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: hope; the rules may be negotiable.

chapters.title: Ansel's Thirty Years
chapters.summary: Ansel confesses everything: how he escaped the lag as a boy by trading his sister's name, and has fed the school memories ever since to keep her asleep. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: shame meeting forgiveness he doesn't believe he deserves.

chapters.title: The Solstice Approaches
chapters.summary: Mirrors across the village begin lagging; the school is leaking. Staff who can't see the truth start packing. Theo finds the torn ledger page hidden in Ansel's toolbox—he's had the ending all along. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: betrayal, then understanding of why he hid it.

chapters.title: Marked Absent
chapters.summary: The headmistress, furious at Theo's interference, marks Theo absent in the register—and Theo begins fading from photographs and colleagues' memories. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: erasure as body horror; invisibility was her wish, now weaponized.

chapters.title: Into the Lag
chapters.summary: Ansel holds Theo's fading hand and speaks her name into the mirror, anchoring her long enough for her to step through the glass into the held classroom. POV: both. Emotional beat: love as literal anchor against oblivion.

chapters.title: The Classroom That Never Rang
chapters.summary: Inside the lag: a lesson suspended since 1893, chalk dust hanging mid-air. Theo meets the seven, including Ansel's sister Wren, awake and furious at being kept. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: righteous anger of the forgotten.

chapters.title: The Founder's Mistake
chapters.summary: Confronting the headmistress across two realities, Theo proves the ritual fails because it demands taking; names must be offered. The headmistress, unraveling, refuses to release her claim. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: climax of wills—compassion versus possession.

chapters.title: A Name Freely Given
chapters.summary: At the solstice bell, Theo writes her own name in the ledger under 'Invited,' and Ansel adds his beside hers. The ritual inverts; the lag collapses inward. POV: both. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into vow—love against duty, duty rewritten.

chapters.title: Morning Roll Call
chapters.summary: Twenty-nine students answer Theo's register, including Wren, aged but alive. The headmistress is gone; the school remembers her only as a portrait. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: exhausted, improbable joy.

chapters.title: Every Mirror but One
chapters.summary: The cost surfaces: no mirror anywhere will show Theo's face—except the old corridor glass, which shows her clearly, always, one second early now, as if anticipating her. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: bittersweet acceptance of a scarred victory.

chapters.title: Ansel and the Visitor
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ansel's POV: term ends, and Theo stays—not trapped, but choosing, teaching the formerly held children while Ansel retires his nightly feeding. The last line: the house isn't lonely anymore. Emotional beat: homecoming; found family sealed in ordinary routine.
